key_insight: The paper unifies multiple “butterfly effect” regimes in turbulence—standard chaos, Eulerian spontaneous stochasticity, Lagrangian spontaneous stochasticity, and localized perturbations—through the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent (FSLE).
engineering_relevance: It helps define practical forecast limits in high-Reynolds-number flows, which matters for turbulence modeling, control, and uncertainty quantification.
method: Use FSLE to measure perturbation growth as a function of scale.
Analyze a Sabra shell model with added thermal noise to connect Lyapunov and large-scale regimes.
Use the Kraichnan model to illustrate Lagrangian spontaneous stochasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a synthesis supported by FSLE-based analysis of the Sabra shell model and the Kraichnan model, rather than a single data-driven benchmark.
watch_item: The results are model-based and conceptual, so direct transfer to real-world turbulent flows may require careful validation and parameter matching.
paper_title: The real butterfly effect: from the pop culture to mathematics and physics
